newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Kuala Lumpur shares end mixed, situationals active.
newsitem.headline: Kuala Lumpur shares end mixed, situationals active.

text.p: Proton surged ahead while Sungei Way fell out of favour in trading dominated by situational stocks and secondary issues.
At the close, the key Composite Index was up 0.06 of a point to 1,097.54. The Second Board index fell 2.24 to 575.92.
Dealers and analysts said carmaker Proton saw heavy buying on expectations it would post strong earnings for the year ended March 31, 1997, to be reported later on Friday.
"The results must be good. They are still doing well," said an institutional salesman at a Singapore brokerage. The stock jumped 90 cents to 13.60 ringgit.
Analysts said there were rumours that Proton would report pretax earnings of 1.0 billion ringgit, above market forecasts.
The stock of Proton's parent firm, Hicom, which was also scheduled to release its results on Friday, was unchanged at 5.0 ringgit.

Construction firm Sungei Way plunged 58 cents to a 12-month low of 4.36 ringgit, on investor concerns it may have paid too much for a stake in Gopeng. Gopeng was down two cents to 4.84. "Sungei Way fell out of bed...on its Gopeng stake," said G.K. Goh Stockbrokers.
